title: Smart Agriculture UGM Researchers Study AI and Robotics Innovation at Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 at WUR
excerpt: Wageningen, the Netherlands — Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho and Muhammad Athala Fawwaz Dzaky from the Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC), Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), participated in the Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 at Wageningen University & Research (WUR). This participation was part of a series of staff mobility activities from the International Joint Research Academy (IJRA) and student mobility from the International Joint Supervision Program (IJSP) held on 1–12 September 2026.
body:
**Wageningen, the Netherlands —** Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho and Muhammad Athala Fawwaz Dzaky from the Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC), Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), participated in the Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 at Wageningen University & Research (WUR). This participation was part of a series of staff mobility activities from the International Joint Research Academy (IJRA) and student mobility from the International Joint Supervision Program (IJSP) held on 1–12 September 2026.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1039-1-screenshot-2026-09-17-at-21.43.04-1030x762.webp)

Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 took place on 10 September 2026 from 09.00–15.30 at the Omnia Building, Wageningen Campus. According to [official WUR information](https://www.wur.nl/nl/activiteit/vijfde-vision-robotics-parcours), this event was the fifth edition of a biennial gathering that brings together the agri-foodtech sector, researchers, technology developers, end-users, and various stakeholders. The event was designed to introduce the latest developments in artificial intelligence, sensor technology, and robotic systems, while discussing their role in supporting global food provision and nature conservation.

During the event, participants took a campus tour to sensor and robotics system laboratories organized across eight innovation stations. Technologies introduced included selective and automated harvesting systems, smart sensor technology, autonomous systems, simulation and digital twins, smart equipment for the agrifood sector, and the application of artificial intelligence and machine vision. The event program also provided spaces for technology demonstrations, discussions with experts, and networking among participants. The theme and program overview were also published by [NLrobotics](https://www.nlrobotics.nl/agenda/vision-robotics-parcours-2026).

For Dr. Andri and Athala, this event provided an opportunity to directly observe the direction of modern agricultural technology development. The various technologies displayed had connections with SARC UGM's research focus, particularly spectral imaging, plant phenotyping, indoor farming, precision agriculture, artificial intelligence, and agricultural robotics. Exposure to systems developed and demonstrated at WUR provided insight into technology readiness levels, system operations, and possibilities for application in tropical agricultural research in Indonesia.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1039-2-screenshot-2026-09-17-at-21.49.58-890x1030.webp)

Participation in Vision + Robotics Parcours also served as a useful technology scouting process and research capacity comparison. UGM researchers could identify relevant technologies for adaptation, determine components still requiring development, and establish priorities for facilities and competencies needed. This knowledge could serve as a foundation for designing experiments, developing prototypes, updating learning materials, and determining student research topics aligned with global technological developments.

The event also demonstrated the importance of relationships among higher education institutions, research institutions, technology developers, industry partners, and end-users. For SARC UGM, this collaboration model provided a reference for building research that does not stop at concept development but is directed toward testing, refinement, and application of technology according to field needs. Meetings with researchers and technology practitioners also opened opportunities for networking to exchange knowledge, co-develop proposals, produce collaborative publications, and develop research partnerships in the future.

An important implication of this participation is the availability of an initial framework for developing a roadmap for smart agricultural technology development at UGM. Technologies observed do not necessarily need to be applied directly in the same form but can be examined based on tropical commodity needs, environmental conditions, infrastructure readiness, costs, and user capacity in Indonesia. This approach enables SARC UGM to select the most relevant innovations and develop them into appropriate solutions.

The experience of participating in Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 strengthened the learning journey of Dr. Andri and Athala during their stay at WUR. Beyond gaining insights into cutting-edge technology, both gained understanding of an innovation ecosystem that brings together research, education, industry, and community needs. This knowledge is expected to be followed up through research agendas, capacity development for researchers and students, and UGM–WUR collaboration in the field of smart agriculture.

This participation supports the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 2 on Zero Hunger, SDG 4 on Quality Education, SDG 9 on Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, and SDG 17 on Partnerships for the Goals.

original.body:
**Wageningen, Belanda —** Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho dan Muhammad Athala Fawwaz Dzaky dari Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC), Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), mengikuti Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 di Wageningen University & Research (WUR). Keikutsertaan tersebut menjadi bagian dari rangkaian kegiatan _staff mobility_ International Joint Research Academy (IJRA) dan _student mobility_ International Joint Supervision Program (IJSP) yang berlangsung pada 1–12 September 2026.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1039-1-screenshot-2026-09-17-at-21.43.04-1030x762.webp)

Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 diselenggarakan pada 10 September 2026 pukul 09.00–15.30 di Gedung Omnia, Wageningen Campus. Berdasarkan [informasi resmi WUR](https://www.wur.nl/nl/activiteit/vijfde-vision-robotics-parcours), kegiatan ini merupakan edisi kelima dari acara dua tahunan yang mempertemukan sektor _agri-foodtech_, peneliti, pengembang teknologi, pengguna akhir, dan berbagai pemangku kepentingan. Acara ini dirancang untuk memperkenalkan perkembangan terbaru dalam kecerdasan buatan, teknologi sensor, dan sistem robotika, sekaligus membahas perannya dalam mendukung penyediaan pangan global dan konservasi alam.

Dalam kegiatan tersebut, peserta mengikuti tur kampus menuju laboratorium sensor dan sistem robotika yang disusun dalam delapan stasiun inovasi. Sejumlah teknologi yang diperkenalkan mencakup sistem pemanenan selektif dan otomatis, teknologi sensor cerdas, sistem otonom, simulasi dan _digital twins_, peralatan cerdas untuk sektor agrifood, serta penerapan kecerdasan buatan dan _machine vision_. Rangkaian acara juga menyediakan ruang demonstrasi teknologi, diskusi bersama para ahli, dan jejaring antarpeserta. Gambaran tema dan program tersebut turut dipublikasikan oleh [NLrobotics](https://www.nlrobotics.nl/agenda/vision-robotics-parcours-2026).

Bagi Dr. Andri dan Athala, kegiatan ini memberikan kesempatan untuk melihat secara langsung arah perkembangan teknologi pertanian modern. Berbagai teknologi yang ditampilkan memiliki keterkaitan dengan fokus penelitian SARC UGM, khususnya _spectral imaging_, _plant phenotyping_, _indoor farming_, pertanian presisi, kecerdasan buatan, dan robotika pertanian. Paparan terhadap sistem yang telah dikembangkan dan didemonstrasikan di WUR memberikan gambaran mengenai tingkat kesiapan teknologi, cara kerja sistem, serta kemungkinan penerapannya pada penelitian pertanian tropis di Indonesia.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1039-2-screenshot-2026-09-17-at-21.49.58-890x1030.webp)

Keikutsertaan dalam Vision + Robotics Parcours juga bermanfaat sebagai proses _technology scouting_ dan pembandingan kapasitas riset. Peneliti UGM dapat mengidentifikasi teknologi yang relevan untuk diadaptasi, menentukan komponen yang masih perlu dikembangkan, serta menyusun prioritas fasilitas dan kompetensi yang dibutuhkan. Pengetahuan tersebut dapat menjadi dasar dalam merancang eksperimen, mengembangkan prototipe, memperbarui materi pembelajaran, dan menentukan topik penelitian mahasiswa yang sesuai dengan perkembangan teknologi global.

Acara ini juga memperlihatkan pentingnya hubungan antara perguruan tinggi, institusi riset, pengembang teknologi, mitra industri, dan pengguna akhir. Bagi SARC UGM, model kolaborasi tersebut memberikan referensi untuk membangun penelitian yang tidak berhenti pada pengembangan konsep, tetapi diarahkan menuju pengujian, penyempurnaan, dan penerapan teknologi sesuai kebutuhan lapangan. Pertemuan dengan peneliti dan pelaku teknologi turut membuka peluang jejaring untuk pertukaran pengetahuan, penyusunan proposal bersama, publikasi kolaboratif, serta pengembangan kemitraan riset pada masa mendatang.

Implikasi penting dari keikutsertaan ini adalah tersedianya gambaran awal untuk menyusun peta jalan pengembangan teknologi pertanian cerdas di UGM. Teknologi yang diamati tidak harus diterapkan secara langsung dalam bentuk yang sama, tetapi dapat dikaji berdasarkan kebutuhan komoditas tropis, kondisi lingkungan, kesiapan infrastruktur, biaya, dan kemampuan pengguna di Indonesia. Pendekatan tersebut memungkinkan SARC UGM memilih inovasi yang paling relevan dan mengembangkannya menjadi solusi yang tepat guna.

Pengalaman mengikuti Vision + Robotics Parcours 2026 memperkuat rangkaian pembelajaran Dr. Andri dan Athala selama berada di WUR. Selain memperoleh wawasan tentang teknologi terkini, keduanya mendapatkan pemahaman mengenai ekosistem inovasi yang mempertemukan riset, pendidikan, industri, dan kebutuhan masyarakat. Pengetahuan ini diharapkan dapat ditindaklanjuti melalui agenda penelitian, pengembangan kapasitas peneliti dan mahasiswa, serta kerja sama UGM–WUR dalam bidang pertanian cerdas.

Partisipasi tersebut mendukung Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan, khususnya SDG 2 tentang Tanpa Kelaparan, SDG 4 tentang Pendidikan Berkualitas, SDG 9 tentang Industri, Inovasi, dan Infrastruktur, serta SDG 17 tentang Kemitraan untuk Mencapai Tujuan.
